'''Onsen-ji''' (温泉寺) is a {{ill|Rinzai school|en|Rinzai school|qid=Q639625|lt=Rinzai|1=Rinzai school}} Buddhist temple affiliated with the [[Myoshin-ji]] branch, located in the city of {{ill|Suwa, Nagano|en|Suwa, Nagano|qid=Q846338|lt=Suwa|1=Suwa, Nagano}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture|1=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. The temple's mountain name is Rinjozan (臨江山), and its principal deity is [[:en:Yakushi Nyorai|Yakushi Nyorai]] (Bhaisajyaguru). It serves as the 7th station of the [[Chubu 49 Yakushi Pilgrimage]] and the 24th station of the [[Suwa 33 Kannon Pilgrimage]].

== History ==
Onsen-ji was established in {{ill|1640|en|1640|qid=Q6901|lt=1640|1=1640}} (Kan'ei 17) by the second lord of {{ill|Takamatsu Domain|en|Takamatsu Domain|qid=Q1036915|lt=Takamatsu|1=Takamatsu Domain}}, [[:en:Suwa Tadatsune|Suwa Tadatsune]], to safeguard the {{ill|Onsen|en|Onsen|qid=Q655311|lt=Onsen|1=Onsen}} sources of the area. The founding monk, [[Tairei Genmi]], was invited from the [[Jiun-ji Temple|Jiun-ji]] in {{ill|Shimosuwa|en|Shimosuwa|qid=Q1204211|lt=Shimosuwa|1=Shimosuwa}}. The temple became the family temple of the Suwa clan, with the graves of eight generations of clan heads, from [[:en:Suwa Tadatsune|Suwa Tadatsune]] to {{ill|Suwa Tadamasa|en|Suwa Tadamasa|qid=Q11631883|lt=Suwa Tadamasa|1=Suwa Tadamasa}}.

After a fire in 1870 (Meiji 3), which destroyed its main structures, the temple's gates, Noh stage, and Yakui-mon were relocated from {{ill|Takamatsu Castle|en|Takamatsu Castle|qid=Q1305872|lt=Takamatsu Castle|1=Takamatsu Castle}} to reconstruct the temple grounds. The site also features a statue by {{ill|Mokujiki|en|Mokujiki|qid=Q104876072|lt=Mokujiki|1=Mokujiki}}, stone statues by [[Moriya Teiji]], and a bronze bell believed to have been repurposed from the {{ill|Battle of Nagashino|en|Battle of Nagashino|qid=Q428369|lt=Battle of Nagashino|1=Battle of Nagashino}}.

The temple's location on a hill offers panoramic views of {{ill|Lake Suwa|en|Lake Suwa|qid=Q1206692|lt=Lake Suwa|1=Lake Suwa}} and the surrounding hot spring town.

== Cultural Assets ==
* '''National Historic Site''': Takamatsu Clan Graveyard (jointly designated with [[Raigaku-ji]])
* '''Suwa City Cultural Property''': Onsen-ji Iron Pagoda (a multi-storied pagoda used for relics)
* '''City Cultural Property''': The pagoda and Noh stage are both historical assets of regional significance.

== Access ==
Onsen-ji is a 15-minute walk from {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=JR|1=East Japan Railway Company}} {{ill|Chūō Main Line|en|Chūō Main Line|qid=Q1078110|lt=Chūō Main Line|1=Chūō Main Line}}'s [[Kamisuwa Station]].
